parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs one of the most protective subnational environments documented (shield law for care, gender-identity non-discrimination since 1993, X-marker licences, hate-crime coverage, trans-panic defence abolished, no facility ban) against a national layer with universal-exposure exposures at every entry point: binary sex marker enforcement, the February 2025 refusal cable with fraud/misrepresentation findings, documented passport confiscations stranding travellers, and foreign-government advisories. State protections cannot reach the border desk, national custody, or federal prosecution; the operative entry interaction is hostile. Custody placement by birth sex is documented at state level, dated 2012. Care access is protected locally, including travelling families. Severity if outed at entry is administrative refusal or fraud ineligibility, not imprisonment; escalation pathways into national custody are documented as abusive. Result sits above high-risk anchors but below fully-functioning-remedy tiers.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports/visas enforce birth-sex binary; X markers stopped; Feb 2025 cable directs refusal on document discrepancies and consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility for suspected misrepresentation; travellers report confiscated passports and stranding.
entry_documents.protection: X passports remain valid until expiration; ACLU litigation pending; legal-aid FAQ exists; limited waiver possible for fraud findings.
entry_documents.interaction: Visa adjudication under national rules occurs regardless of destination state; a discrepancy can escalate to refusal or fraud finding.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau 2026 policies mandate hair-cutting, hormone removal and forced psychiatric therapy for trans inmates; immigration custody shows forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse of trans men; state prison placement by birth sex documented (2012 assault case).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented as operating for visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any national arrest or detention escalation places the visitor in the abusive national custody regime.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans access to federally funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; facility bans in many other state/provinces, criminal trespass in 4.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province has no documented facility ban and sits in the most-protective tier; non-discrimination law covers public accommodations since 1993.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility access is state-governed locally, but federal facilities follow national rules.

care_services.exposure: National hostility: care for minors described as 'mutilation' by executive order; hospitals subpoenaed nationally; proposed insurance bars.
care_services.protection: 2023 shield law blocks out-of-state warrants, subpoenas, extradition and custody removals; public insurance covers trans care; insurers barred from exclusions; conversion therapy banned.
care_services.interaction: Travelling families seeking care fall inside shield protection; national actors could still pursue parallel routes.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders frame gender ideology as extremist threat; counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; bathroom-arrest precedent in another state/province.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Local law treats gender identity as a protected category; trans panic defence abolished; hate-crime enhancements in force.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National threat-framing could influence enforcement posture, though state law enforcement operates under protective state law.

minors_guardians.exposure: Teachers criminally prosecute-able nationally for facilitating social transition; care for minors banned in 27 other state/provinces; national records subpoenas target under-19 patients.
minors_guardians.protection: Shield law prevents out-of-state custody removals for care obtained locally; state care and conversion-therapy protections cover minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor's care is shielded locally; national investigators or another state's courts remain the residual risk.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific violence data; only dated 2012 custody assault documented; national hate-crime coverage exists but patchy at state level nationally.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime law since 1993; non-discrimination enforcement in public accommodations; most-protective tier rating by external assessment.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police operate under protective state law; enforcement data not sourced.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Shield law never applied in decided cases on this record; no state enforcement data for hate-crime or discrimination provisions; no state violence figures.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National injunctions blocking several orders; litigation pending; state legal infrastructure (1993 statutes, tribunals) on paper and partially operating.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies against national measures run through national courts, slow and unresolved; state remedies untested in documented cases.

anchor_checks.comparison: Less severe than 0.35-A: no visitor register, no exclusion regime, no agency-only appeals. The visitor can enter and live locally under protective state law; the national exposure is document-based and administrative, not a universal conduct register.

Comparable to 0.55-B's border-friction core but materially harsher: not just secondary screening but directed refusals, a fraud ineligibility lever, documented stranded travellers, and a custody regime below with documented abuse. Sits somewhat below that anchor.

Below 0.75-C: that anchor has respectful trained border officers and functioning tribunals. Here border policy is affirmatively hostile with no documented visitor-facing remedy; local protections cannot offset a national entry regime that every traveller passes through.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is bifurcated: locally, the traveller enjoys shelter-law protection for care, anti-discrimination coverage, identity-document openness and no facility ban — a genuinely protective layer including travelling families. But the national layer is a universal-exposure exposure at the only unavoidable stage of the journey: every entry forces a binary sex marker, discrepancies trigger directed refusal and possible lifetime fraud findings, and passports have been confiscated. If anything escalates to national arrest, detention or immigration custody, documented conditions are abusive. Severity if outed at entry is administrative (refusal, stranding, fraud bar) rather than imprisonment, keeping this above the 0.35 band; but the hostile national custody and threat-framing layers, and the inability of state protections to reach the border, keep it well below the 0.75 band.
